title: Each kb MCP write tool carries the annotation of one documented table, sets no force-prompt flag, and a Bash deny rule of the clone's or the user's settings refuses its command line
goal: kb/_self/plugin.md holds one table of every backlog write and job tool with its readOnlyHint (false), destructiveHint (true for set, drop, close and kb_job_cancel, which replace or delete; false for the rest), idempotentHint and openWorldHint (true for land, dispatch and begin, which reach a git remote or start a model session), and tools/list carries exactly those annotations; no tool sets _meta anthropic/requiresUserInteraction, which would deny the call in an unattended headless run; the Bash deny-rule mirror that kb_backlog_write applies (bash_denied) applies to every write and job tool for the command line python3 _tools/backlog.py VERB ARGS and also reads the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json deny rules, so a Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py drop *) rule refuses backlog_drop; the docs say what the mirror still misses (a managed policy's rules)

run: import sys,os,tempfile,json;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");os.environ["KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS"]="1";h=tempfile.mkdtemp();os.makedirs(h+"/.claude");open(h+"/.claude/settings.json","w").write(json.dumps({"permissions":{"deny":["Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py drop *)"]}}));os.environ["HOME"]=h;import kb_mcp;want={"backlog_claim":(0,1),"backlog_release":(0,0),"backlog_answer":(0,0),"backlog_set":(1,1),"backlog_move":(0,1),"backlog_reopen":(0,0),"backlog_drop":(1,0),"backlog_new":(0,0),"backlog_gate_add":(0,1),"backlog_land":(0,1),"backlog_done":(0,0),"backlog_stage_back":(0,1),"backlog_dispatch":(0,0),"backlog_begin":(0,0),"backlog_close":(1,0),"kb_job_cancel":(1,1)};tools={t["name"]:t for t in kb_mcp.tool_list()};missing=[n for n in want if n not in tools];assert not missing,missing;bad=[n for n,(d,i) in want.items() if tools[n]["annotations"].get("readOnlyHint") is not False or bool(tools[n]["annotations"].get("destructiveHint"))!=bool(d) or bool(tools[n]["annotations"].get("idempotentHint"))!=bool(i)];assert not bad,bad;assert tools["kb_job"]["annotations"]["readOnlyHint"] is True;assert not [n for n,t in tools.items() if "anthropic/requiresUserInteraction" in (t.get("_meta") or {})],"force-prompt flag set";r=kb_mcp.handle({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"backlog_drop","arguments":{"id":"ST-abcdefgh","why":"x"}}})["result"];assert r["isError"] and "deny" in r["content"][0]["text"].lower(),r

gates.question: Which permission rule do the kb MCP write tools run under in this clone, where settings.json allows the whole mcp__kb server?
options: Add an ask rule for backlog_drop, backlog_close and kb_job_cancel
Replace the blanket allow with a list of read tools and ask for every write tool
gates.reason: because Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py *) is already allowed without a prompt and an ask rule denies the same call in an unattended headless run

notes: Evidence 2026-11-08. Claude Code (docs mcp.md and permissions.md): allow/ask/deny take mcp__server__tool, evaluated deny, ask, allow; settings files skip mcp__ rules with parentheses, so no argument-level rule exists. The annotations the docs name: readOnlyHint (calls run in parallel with other read-only calls) and idempotentHint (a pending call may be repeated once after a closed connection, HTTP servers only); destructiveHint is not named, so it informs a person and no rule. _meta anthropic/requiresUserInteraction true forces a prompt on every call even in bypassPermissions and with an allow rule, and in dontAsk or non-interactive mode it denies: unusable for the unattended runners that land and close, so none sets it. This clone's .claude/settings.json allows the whole mcp__kb server (so coord_claim and the write tools run without a prompt: ST-wqbibuy6 holds that decision for the coord tools) and Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py *); its deny list names no backlog command, so bash_denied (kb_mcp.py:1504) mirrors nothing today for the backlog; 211 bash permission.request rows against 35,919 Bash calls, so the Bash route prompts rarely too. The mirror reads only the clone's two settings files (backlog.md:85); a managed policy's deny stays unread. destructiveHint true marks calls that replace or delete (set replaces whole lists, drop deletes an item outside a sprint, close deletes a sprint, cancel stops work); land and stage-back are idempotent by their documented re-runs. The settings.json change an answer to the gate may need is its own follow-up, not in this story's touches. test_redact.py:255-259 must move to this table.
